title.narrative: Improved employment policies and business models to facilitate the adoption of measures towards decent work in selected supply chains and states, targeting vulnerable workers and youth

description.narrative:
In 2024–2025, global uncertainties continued due to armed conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, climate emergencies, and supply chain disruptions. These, combined with post-pandemic effects, inflation, and geopolitical tensions, impacted labour markets and social cohesion.
In Brazil, the government pursued inclusive recovery despite political and fiscal challenges. GDP grew 3.4% in 2024 (BRL¿11.7 trillion or USD¿2.34 trillion), with 2025 growth projected at 2.4%. Employment hit 106.8 million, and unemployment fell to 6.2%. Yet, informality affects 39 million workers (38%), and the average real wage, though improving, is BRL¿3,294 (USD¿660). Inequalities persist among youth, women, and marginalized groups, especially in low-productivity sectors.
In response, the ILO is deepening cooperation with national actors to promote decent work, with a focus on vulnerable groups and youth. The Office supports strategies for formalization, better working conditions, and inclusive growth in key supply chains and regions. This includes technical support for relaunching the Sustainable Work Program, designing a national employment strategy, and promoting responsible business conduct, particularly in BNDES-financed projects (Brazil's development bank).
Efforts also include expanding the SCORE methodology (ILO training programme for small and medium enterprises) in the textile sector, supporting socio-biodiversity business networks, and formalizing informal enterprises. The ILO promotes youth employment through skills training, apprenticeships, and pacts targeting green and digital jobs.
Aligned with Brazil’s Ecological Transformation Plan, the ILO supports sustainable finance, energy transition, and the bioeconomy, contributes to REDD+ implementation (UN climate mechanism), and enhances dialogue with Indigenous Peoples (C169). Cross-cutting efforts strengthen institutions, produce green jobs data, and center gender equality and inclusion in all actions.

sector.narrative: 8.2 Achieve higher levels of economic productivity through diversification, technological upgrading and innovation, including through a focus on highvalue added and labour-intensive sectors

Output 4.3. Increased support for enterprises – especially MSMEs – to achieve decent work and improve productivity
